structure.heading: Macro Environment Outlook and Implications for Capital Allocation (FY2026 Planning Window)
text_content: **Macro Environment Outlook and Implications for Capital Allocation (FY2026 Planning Window)**

U.S. headline inflation remains elevated: CPI inflation was 3.4% in April 2024, while the Federal Reserve target range for the federal funds rate was 5.25%–5.50% throughout 2024. For the FY2026 planning window this sustains a higher cost of capital, pressures discount rates and raises hurdle rates for new investments, increasing emphasis on shorter payback periods and staged capital deployment and tighter liquidity conditions persist.

Corporates should assume sustained elevated borrowing costs and tighter credit spreads when scheduling refinancings and covenant tests. The FY2026 planning window must prioritize liquidity buffers, proactive maturity ladders, and hedging of interest rate and FX exposures. Treasury will run scenario analyses that include base, upside, and stress cases to determine short-term draw capacity and thresholds for discretionary capex deferral and maintain strategic optionality.

The regulatory landscape also influences capital allocation: the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism transitional reporting phase began on 1 October 2023, requiring reported embedded emissions for imports into the EU. This compels targeted capital for supply-chain decarbonization, measurement systems, and potential reshoring or tariff mitigation strategies. Scenario-based carbon pricing and compliance costs must be included in FY2026 investment appraisals and M&A valuation adjustments.

structure.heading: Portfolio Performance Review and Board Decisions Requested on Strategic Options (FY2025–FY2027)
text_content: **Portfolio Performance Review and Board Decisions Requested on Strategic Options (FY2025–FY2027)**

FY2025 portfolio performance delivered resilient top-line growth and margin expansion. Revenue was $12.4B, up 6% year‑over‑year, driven primarily by strength in Cloud & Data Platforms and selective price realization in Services. Enterprise EBITDA margin improved to 18.2% in FY2025 from 16.9% in FY2024, reflecting productivity initiatives, fixed-cost leverage on higher volumes, and disciplined SG&A management. While macro volatility affected timing of some large deals, the portfolio composition shift toward recurring, higher‑margin offerings materially supported profitability. Management has tightened monthly performance reporting and reallocated working capital to sustain cash‑flow stability through the FY2026 planning window. The board can rely on management's disciplined execution through FY2026.

Segment-level results indicate a clear need to rebalance capital toward growth platforms. Cloud & Data Platforms exceeded internal targets in FY2025, while Legacy Products showed lower growth and rising maintenance cost profiles, constraining long-term margin expansion. To accelerate migration and capture TAM expansion, management requests board approval by 30 June 2026 for a $1.2B capital reallocation program from Legacy Products to Cloud & Data Platforms. The proposed program is phased over FY2026–FY2027 with predefined gates, risk limits, and contingency reserves. Expected outcomes include a higher recurring revenue mix, shorter payback on incremental investments, and incremental EBITDA contribution tracked in quarterly KPIs.

Management asks the board to take three specific actions to enable FY2025–FY2027 execution. 1) Approve the $1.2B capital reallocation program, authorizing phase‑gate deployment and reallocations from Legacy Products. 2) Endorse the preferred strategic option set—prioritized investment in Cloud & Data Platforms, selective bolt‑on M&A limited to board‑precleared thresholds, and continued cost optimization in Legacy Products. 3) Delegate authority to the CEO and CFO to implement transfers up to $300M per quarter within governance limits, subject to quarterly reporting on revenue impact, EBITDA progression, and cash‑flow variance to plan. Detailed implementation milestones are attached.
